title: Use `append_` instead of `parse_` for `String` methods.
body:
`String` has various methods like `parse_utf8`. These functions replace the current contents of the string with the contents of a buffer of some encoding.
This PR expands versatility of these methods, to be able to append to existing contents. This makes them more versatile, exemplified by the ability to remove 3 functions of duplicated functionality in `ustring.cpp`.

## Motivation

`parse_` function behavior is somewhat odd: The old string isn't used at all - instead, its contents are fully replaced. 
It is questionable whether it wouldn't be a better fit to just create a new string.

Indeed, most callers look like this:
```c++
String new_string;
new_string.parse_utf8(utf8_buffer);
```

This would be more idiomatic with the factory method:
```c++
String new_string = String::utf8(utf8_buffer);
```

These cases make up a good ~80% of `parse_` callers.
Another ~15% actually does something with the error:
```c++
String new_string;
ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG(new_string.parse_utf8(utf8_buffer), "Failed to parse string.")
```

This would be equivalent to calling `append_` functions:
```c++
String new_string;
ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG(new_string.append_utf8(utf8_buffer), "Failed to parse string.")
```

Finally, there are only a handful of callers that actually want to replace the string in question:
```c++
this->string.parse_utf8(utf8_buffer);
```

They need the (slightly awkward) workaround of clearing the string first:
```c++
this->string.clear();
this->string.append_utf8(utf8_buffer);
// Alternatively, this->string = String::utf8(utf8_buffer);
```

Alright, so "replace" functionality is not used often, so what?
I'd argue that `append_` functionality is useful more often: Basically, append the contents of the buffer to the existing contents. This allows them to be used when combining buffers / string parts, which currently is often performed using the rather slow `+` operator.
De-duplication potential can be seen immediately because `operator+=` functions can be re-implemented by calling `append_`. I may eventually make a follow-up proposal to replace uses of `operator+=` with `append_` calls, because it makes the expected type of encoding more explicit.

In addition, these functions will be usable for `String::concat` eventually (#99929). This will require a few more changes, but this is a necessary refactor step going in the right direction. :)

## Caveats
There is one performance benefit of `parse_xxx`: If there was a previous string of similar length, the existing buffer may be reusable, saving time allocating a new one.

However, given how few callers even use `parse_` for replacing strings, I think this is not important. In addition, this problem would be better solved by implementing `reserve()` for `CowData`, allowing for non-deallocating resize. I am planning to propose this functionality when I make progress with other `CowData` changes.
